The complete June 1959 University of Michigan report UMR1342 was also acquired from the [permanent repository record](https://hdl.han

**Literal source objects and corrected tuple.** For a finite nonempty input alphabet \(I\), an \(I\)-automaton is \((S,f,d,D)\), where **\(S\) is the internal-state set**, \(f:I\times S\to S\), \(d\in S\), and \(D\subseteq S\). The prior note incorrectly called \(S\) the input alphabet. The behavior \(T(\mathfrak A)\) is the set of finite input words whose unique run from \(d\) ends in \(D\), including the empty word exactly when \(d\in D\) ([journal pp. 21--22](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1961-0139530-9)). Formula, finite-set assignment, characteristic-column word, run, and accepted language remain distinct objects.

**Theorem 5.3 and both proof directions.** In \(L_1^1\), individuals range over natural numbers and monadic variables over finite sets. An \(r\)-tuple of finite sets is encoded by its columns in \(U_r=\{0,1\}^r\), cut after the last nonzero column; admissible words are \(U_r^*U_r^0\cup\{\Lambda\}\). Theorem 5.3(a) effectively maps every formula to a regular language of satisfying encodings. Lemmas 5.4--5.5 put set quantifiers outside individual quantifiers and reduce the matrix to Boolean combinations of local successor patterns; Boolean operations are regular operations, and finite-set existential quantification is coordinate projection followed by the right truncation established in Lemma

**Arithmetic and design consequences.** Corollary 5.8 decides \(L_1^1\) truth by regular-language emptiness. Section 5.9 uses \(\tau(F)=\sum_{k\in F}2^k\) and a finite carry set to recover Presburger decidability; §§5.10--5.16 give richer decidable finite/cofinite-set presentations over \(\mathbb N\) and \(\mathbb Z\). For finite behavior, an \(A/B\)-automaton is \((S,f,d,g)\) with \(f:A\times S\to S\) and \(g:S\to B\). Theorem 7.1 says its behaviors are exactly the regular, prefix-closed, output-functional, input-total paired-word languages. Lemma 6.1 constructs the largest strongly \(A\)-extendable regular sublanguage \(\gamma_A\subseteq\gamma\); Theorem 8.1 gives a realizing transducer wi

**Published correction and negative boundary.** Printed §8.6.2 falsely collapses a finite union of local infinite-sequence languages to one relation language. The 1962 errata replaces it by \(S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_k\), with \(k\) not necessarily one, then gives a disjoint-tag construction whose projection is that union; §8.6.3 can then reduce the restricted arbitrary-set specification to Theorem 8.1. The reader uses only this corrected route. Chapter IV separately encodes Post normal-system proofs: Theorem 10.2 makes finite-predicate satisfiability recursively enumerable but undecidable of maximal r.e. degree, and Corollary 10.6 separates decidable satisfaction by a fixed input-free automaton
